newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rail intermodal freight surges - AAR.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rail intermodal freight surges - AAR.

text.p: U.S. and Canadian freight rail traffic was up in the week ended July 5 compared to the same week last year despite the Fourth of July holiday in the United States and the Canada Day holiday on July 1, Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR said U.S. carloads rose 2.1 percent in the week to 291,684 from 285,675 in the year-ago week, while ton-miles were up 2.8 percent to 22.1 in the week from 21.5 a year ago. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, is one ton of freight hauled one mile.
Several sectors reported double-digit gains in loadings, including in farm products other than grains, which surged 45.7 percent in the July 5 week compared to the year-ago week.

Other increases were seen in container loadings, which were up 16.7 percent, trailers, up 13.1 percent, motor vehicles and equipment, up 16.5 percent, metals and products, up 11.5 percent, lumber and wood products, up 13.5 percent, and primary forest products, up 13.3 percent.

A few sectors saw a decrease in carloads, including coke, which was down 8.1 percent from the year-ago week, metallic ores, which were down 6.0 percent, and nonmetallic minerals, which were down 5.5 percent.
U.S. intermodal traffic rose 15.2 percent to 147,902 in the week ended July 5 compared to 128,366 in the same week last year.

AAR reported that the two Canadian transcontinental railroads had 46,942 carloads in the July 5 week, up 17.2 percent from the year-ago week, and 22,931 trailers and containers, up 15.6 percent from last year.

Combined U.S. and Canada carloadings in the first 27 weeks of 1997 were 10.55 million, up 1.7 percent from the comparable period last year. Combined intermodal traffic was up 7.6 percent to 5.04 trailers and containers.
